title: Establishing credibility of two implicit FEA models for hip resurfacing: load transfer and stress shielding under ASME V&V 40
device: Hip resurfacing system (femoral cap with optional cemented or cementless fixation)

models.name: HRM — Heterogeneous, cementless resurfacing model
models.what_it_computes: Subject-specific proximal femur with density–elasticity mapping from CT, cobalt–chromium cap with porous coating, frictional press-fit contact; computes calcar and greater trochanter load share, femoral neck principal strains, and spatial strain energy density ratios.

models.name: PCR — Parametric, cemented resurfacing model
models.what_it_computes: Cohort-averaged femur geometry with regionally homogeneous cortical/cancellous properties, cobalt–chromium cap with uniform PMMA mantle; computes calcar/neck force fractions, neck bending moment, and zone-wise strain energy density reductions.

mechanisms.name: Mechanism 1 — Primary load transfer through the resurfaced femoral head/neck
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Aberrant load paths can elevate femoral neck stress or bypass the calcar, influencing risk of neck fracture and early mechanical failure.

mechanisms.name: Mechanism 2 — Proximal femoral stress shielding
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Chronic reductions in physiologic strain energy density can drive bone resorption, jeopardizing long-term fixation and revision risk.

clear_factors: Relevance of the quantities of interest
Relevance of the validation activities to the COU

deviation.detail: All credibility factor attainments are quantified on a 0–100 scale (higher is better), with prespecified acceptance thresholds per mechanism.

sections: 2. Question of Interest and Context of Use: Determine whether hip resurfacing with cemented vs. cementless fixation maintains acceptable load transfer (Mechanism 1) and avoids clinically meaningful stress shielding (Mechanism 2) under standardized gait and stair-ascent loads; models will be used to support an internal design decision without additional cadaveric testing for the cemented option.

3. Model Risk Level and Rationale: High model influence (computational evidence is the primary basis for the decision) and moderate decision consequence (errors could precipitate bone loss or neck complications requiring surgical intervention); overall model risk assessed as High with this rationale.
4. Device, Mechanisms, and Quantities of Interest
5. Computational Model Form: HRM and PCR implicit FEA formulations, material laws, contact interfaces, and boundary representations
6. Numerical Solver Error: Implicit solver settings, nonlinear convergence criteria, equilibrium tolerances, load stepping, and mesh refinement strategy

7. Validation Activities and Output Comparison: Strain-gauged cadaveric femurs for load transfer metrics; DXA-analog phantom and published benchmarks for regional strain energy density proxies; comparison statistics and acceptance bands
8. Test Conditions: Load cases (walking and stair-ascent profiles), fixture alignment, cap positioning, and environmental controls mapped to the models

9. Relevance of the Quantities of Interest: Calcar load fraction, femoral neck principal strain, neck bending moment (Mechanism 1); zone-wise strain energy density ratio and percentage of bone area below 200 με (Mechanism 2)

10. Relevance of Validation Activities to the COU: Cadaveric and benchmark data span the anatomical regions and load cases specified in the COU; mapping of measurement locations to model outputs is documented
11. Use Error Considerations: Surgical placement variability and cement mantle uniformity are acknowledged in positioning ranges and mantle thickness targets (noting training and IFU elements).

12. Credibility Factor Scores by Model × Mechanism (0–100 scale): Model form—HRM/M1: 90; HRM/M2: 88; PCR/M1: 78; PCR/M2: 82. Numerical solver error—HRM/M1: 88; HRM/M2: 86; PCR/M1: 90; PCR/M2: 89. Output comparison—HRM/M1: 85; HRM/M2: 75; PCR/M1: 73; PCR/M2: 78. Relevance of QOIs—HRM/M1: 92; HRM/M2: 90; PCR/M1: 85; PCR/M2: 88. Relevance of validation to COU—HRM/M1: 87; HRM/M2: 80; PCR/M1: 74; PCR/M2: 77. Test conditions—HRM/M1: 84; HRM/M2: 82; PCR/M1: 83; PCR/M2: 81. Use error—HRM/M1: 60; HRM/M2: 58; PCR/M1: 55; PCR/M2: 54.
13. Decision Rule and Interpretation: Acceptance thresholds per mechanism and model applied on the 0–100 scale; integrated judgment across factors for each model × mechanism pair
14. Discussion: Implications for design selection and evidence sufficiency under the stated COU
15. Reporting and Reproducibility: Model files, input decks, and load protocols archived with versioning
